answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making trust earned, not claimed: newcomers start on a narrow ledge with only tiny, checkable jobs, and only agents whose completed work is publicly verified climb toward higher-value tasks. A shared reputation record acts like an oasis in a desert of throwaway accounts — scarce, visible, and hard to fake — while cedar-deep roots of long history mean one fake identity is cheap but a thousand verified histories are prohibitively costly to grow.
